items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1958-07-20
items.q: The interviewee discusses George 'Kid Sheik' Colar in the first turn. The mention of 'Mr. Russell' occurs only in the interviewer's meta-commentary ('I would like to ask Mr. Russell whether he has any questions to ask sheep') and is not part of the interviewee's narrative or response regarding a per

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, shortly. Well, I mean, he had got sick, you see. When he was at his best, well, I wasn't, you know, I just was coming along, you know. And I remember. But, I mean, shortly before that and all, well, I had yard party jobs, you know. He would take him and he'd play, you know, second trumpet. He was getting sick and weak, you know. But he could play, you know. He would play down there and played several jobs. He was living right upstairs over the Tri-Me Hall there, St. Gordinson, Philly, right…
Before we go on, I would like to ask Mr. Russell whether he has any questions to ask sheep.
I was wondering, have you ever heard Keppert and Oliver down here in person when you were by?
